name: Dwelling house / secondary dwelling
checks: Height and siting against QDC MP1.1/1.2 and City Plan (small lot code under 450 m²)
Character overlay may control demolition and design

name: Dual occupancy (duplex)
checks: Minimum lot size for dual occupancy in the zone/precinct
Car parking and access for 2 dwellings

name: Multiple dwellings (townhouses / apartments)
checks: Minimum site area and frontage for multiple dwellings
Height, site cover, setbacks and communal open space (Multiple dwelling code)
Car parking rates: Transport, access, parking and servicing planning scheme policy
Infrastructure charges

name: Subdivision (reconfiguring a lot)
checks: Minimum lot size, frontage and development rectangle (Subdivision code)
Rear lot access handle width
Services connections for each new lot (Urban Utilities, Energex)
Survey plan by a registered surveyor; compliance assessment for the plan of subdivision

name: Shop / office / food and drink
term: Shop, Office, Food and drink outlet
checks: Centre hierarchy and gross floor area limits
Car parking and servicing
Amenity: hours, noise, lighting

name: Industry / warehouse
term: Low impact industry, Medium impact industry, Warehouse
checks: Separation from sensitive uses
Environmentally relevant activity (ERA) triggers
Heavy vehicle access and servicing

name: Data centre
term: Research and technology industry (how Queensland planning schemes usually classify data centres – confirm against City Plan Schedule 1 definitions)

sources.name: Sunshine Coast Council – data centres defined as Research and Technology Industry (Sept 2026)
Western Downs – data centre lodged as MCU for Research and Technology Industry, impact assessable

checks: Use term: Research and technology industry. Level of assessment depends on zone; outside industry zones expect impact assessment (public notification)

Power: early Energex / Powerlink connection enquiry; large loads may need a substation or easement. Federal expectations (2026) ask new large data centres to match demand with new renewable generation and pay connection costs

Backup generators: emissions and noise modelling; diesel or gas generation and fuel storage may trigger environmentally relevant activities (check ERA thresholds in Environmental Protection Regulation 2019, Schedule 2 – e.g. electricity generation, fuel burning, chemical storage) needing an environmental authority from DESI
Noise: 24/7 cooling plant and generator testing against Council noise criteria and the Environmental Protection (Noise) Policy
Water/cooling: Urban Utilities water supply capacity and trade waste approval; consider recycled water and low-water cooling
Fire safety: NCC fire engineering, QFES requirements for battery (UPS) rooms and fuel storage; hazardous chemicals (WHS) notifications if thresholds reached
Flood immunity: critical infrastructure usually needs high flood immunity – check flood overlays and FloodWise levels
Interface with residential uses: visual bulk, lighting, setbacks, landscaping
Traffic: construction traffic and heavy vehicle deliveries (generators, transformers)
